D.t: Lynne Walz trails by 5.3 and wins 15% of simulations. Closing it takes about 20,580 voters switching sides, or 41,160 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +11.9 and D +1.3. A normal polling error decides it.

The polls page average is R +4.5. Your best recent poll is Concord Public Opinion Partners for Education Reform Now Advocacy (D) at D +0.3; your worst is Echelon Insights for NetChoice at R +7.3. 8 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Douglas, a projected net 62,942 votes; Lancaster, a projected net 31,391 votes; Sarpy, a projected net 5,364 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Sarpy, D +6.9, 10.0% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Lynne Walz runs furthest behind in Platte, Madison, Washington. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 90% of voters, 41 to 51, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.48 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 69% of voters, 43 to 50, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.46 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 60% of voters, 49 to 43, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.02 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Lynne Walz: Immigration voters 14 to 79, Small counties 25 to 66, Voters who can afford daily costs 36 to 56. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
